title: Etale atlas equalizer for module direct image on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $p:U\to X$ be a surjective etale morphism from an affine scheme $U$. Put $R=U\times_XU$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] with projections $p_1,p_2:R\to U$, and let $a=f\circ p:U\to Y$ and $b=a\circ p_1=a\circ p_2:R\to Y$. For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ on the small etale site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], write $F_U=p^*F$ and $F_R=p_1^*F_U$ (identified with $p_2^*F_U$ by the canonical fibre-product identification). Then the canonical map $f_*F\to a_*F_U$ identifies $f_*F$ with the kernel of the difference of the two restriction maps $a_*F_U\rightrightarrows b_*F_R$ induced by $p_1$ and $p_2$; equivalently, $0\to f_*F\to a_*F_U\rightrightarrows b_*F_R$ is exact at the first two terms in the category of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), proof and displayed exact sequence; the two maps are the restrictions along the projections U \times_X U \rightrightarrows U.

proof.text: Extend $F$ to the enlarged etale site $\mathcal C_X$ as the module sheaf $\widetilde F$ using [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. The same node identifies the canonical ringed-topos map for any morphism $g:A\to Y$ with the continuous functor $V\mapsto A\times_YV$. Direct image is precomposition by that functor, by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3), with scalars restricted along pullback of regular functions. Thus for an etale scheme $V\to Y$ we have $(f_*F)(V)=\widetilde F(X\times_YV)$. Apply the same description also to $a$ and $b$ and their respective modules. These are the canonical direct images of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], since the model supplies precisely the canonical morphisms of ringed topoi, rather than an arbitrary choice of adjoints.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), first four sentences of proof; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H7 and 03G2/03G8 for the enlarged-site and ringed-topos interpretation

proof.text: Fix $V\to Y$ etale from a scheme and put $W=V\times_YX$, $Z=V\times_YU$ and $Q=V\times_YR$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $W$ is an algebraic space and $Z\to W$ is the pullback of the singleton surjective etale covering $U\to X$, hence is a covering. The maps $Z\to U$ and $Q\to R$ are etale, being pullbacks of $V\to Y$, and are schemes by representability. Likewise $R=U\times_XU$ is a scheme and its projections are etale. The base-change and composition assertions of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] put all these objects and maps in the enlarged etale sites in question. In particular $W\to X$ is etale, and $Z\to W$ is a scheme chart to which the sheaf axiom applies.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), covering sentence; base-change geometry is spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F(3)

proof.text: The overlap of this covering is $Z\times_WZ\cong Q$. Indeed a map from a test scheme $T$ into $Z\times_WZ$ is a triple $(v,u_1,u_2)$ with $v:T\to V$, $u_i:T\to U$, $a u_1=a u_2$ equal to the image of $v$ in $Y$, and $p u_1=p u_2$ in $X$. The last equality gives a unique map $r:T\to R$ with projections $u_1,u_2$, and $b r$ is the image of $v$. Thus the triple is exactly a map $T\to V\times_YR$, with the two projections given by $p_1,p_2$. This construction and its inverse commute with test maps, so the fibre-product universal property in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives the asserted canonical isomorphism. The base of the overlap here is $W$, not $X$.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), overlap formula, correcting its printed subscript X to V times_Y X

proof.text: For an etale map, tensor pullback is restriction to the localized etale site by [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. Hence $F_U=p^*F$ is the restriction of $\widetilde F$ to $U$, and $F_R=p_1^*F_U$ is its restriction to $R$; the other restriction along $p_2$ agrees since $p p_1=p p_2$. Using the localization identifications of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], step 1 consequently gives $(a_*F_U)(V)=\widetilde F(Z)$ and $(b_*F_R)(V)=\widetilde F(Q)$. The canonical map from $(f_*F)(V)$ is restriction along $Z\to W$, and the two maps to $(b_*F_R)(V)$ are restriction along the two projections of step 3. The identifications preserve the specified chart projections of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], so they identify the canonical maps, not just the three objects.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), restrictions in the displayed sequence; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LV (lemma-etale-exact-pullback) and equation 03LW (equation-restrict-modules)

proof.text: The equalizer sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), applied to the singleton cover $Z\to W$ and the underlying abelian sheaf of $\widetilde F$, gives injectivity of $\widetilde F(W)\to\widetilde F(Z)$ and a unique antecedent for each $s\in\widetilde F(Z)$ whose two restrictions to $Q$ agree. For abelian groups this condition is exactly that their difference is zero. All maps are $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear: restrictions are semilinear over the structure-sheaf restrictions by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the scalar actions here are induced from the same map to $V$. Thus the sequence of sections is exact at the first two terms as a sequence of $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-modules.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), application of the sheaf condition and displayed sequence (exact at the first two terms only)

proof.text: For a map $V'\to V$ of etale schemes over $Y$, all the maps just constructed are restrictions along the induced fibre-product maps, so functoriality of restriction makes the square for every arrow commute. For a module morphism $F\to G$ the same assertion is its naturality on each chart, as in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. The sequences of step 5 therefore form the stated sequence of module sheaves on $Y$. Kernels of module sheaves are computed sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The sectionwise bijections from $f_*F$ onto the kernel give an isomorphism of module sheaves: their inverses commute with restrictions and addition and scalar multiplication by uniqueness of the sectionwise antecedent. This proves the canonical equalizer assertion and both exactness clauses.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), final sentence: functoriality in V and conclusion

proof_origin.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), full proof; expanded using Properties of Spaces Tags 03H7, 03G2/03G8 and 03LV. The overlap is taken over V times_Y X, correcting the printed subscript X.
